sourceOccurrences.label: Finite forcing certificates
sourceOccurrences.locator: Named statement start lines in the pinned source: 37, 41, 45, 49, 54, 61, 67, 72, 89, 98, 108, 120
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected statement correspondence with scope qualifications
sourceOccurrences.note: OQN6 separates universal forcing from finite certificates. Forcing itself permits arbitrary sets; the accompanying paragraph records membership and intersection consequences without assuming finiteness. X7ET and HRBD give containment, symmetry, monotonicity and the open-witness characterization. Singleton and empty-certificate examples include distinct coordinates, a repeated indispensable coordinate, and the empty coordinate type.

sourceOccurrences.note: Impossible and sure event identities retain their finite-coordinate qualifications. 17DW gives binary-union distribution for increasing events; HP3X gives triple witnesses and associativity. Three distinct singleton witnesses and repeated-coordinate failure are explained. No arbitrary-event associativity is inferred.

sourceOccurrences.note: VMVX includes configuration extension with unchanged exterior, restriction of forcing sets, and the pointwise and event-level equivalences. Neither ambient nor retained coordinates need be finite or countable, and events need not be increasing. The universal forcing restriction works even before imposing finite certificates.

sourceOccurrences.label: Deterministic endpoint laws and BK
sourceOccurrences.locator: Named statement start lines in the pinned source: 29, 35, 42, 49, 56, 67, 73
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected statement correspondence with scope qualifications
sourceOccurrences.note: E7K6 gives the arbitrary-coordinate deterministic law equality and finite-observable endpoint expectations. E7HI gives BK for arbitrary events in finite volume, including mixed zero-one profiles. No increasingness is required there, and no probability-one claim for a possibly nonmeasurable singleton is substituted for measure equality. The empty-coordinate case is included.
